title: The duality, Künneth, Lefschetz and L-function programme
as_he_states: Develop torsion duality, the Künneth formula and Lefschetz; pass to ℓ-adic coefficients; apply the results to L-functions. This is a plan, with no particular rationality assertion on this leaf.
plausible_today: For separated finite-type morphisms in the appropriate invertible-torsion setting, construct Rf!, cup products, trace and duality with their coherence; choose a separate ℓ-adic formalism before forming limits.
state_of_art: SGA4 XVII5.4 (Künneth) and XVIII2–3 (trace and duality), published1973 from the1963–1964 seminar, directly develop the formalism. No exact L-function theorem is assigned to this introductory sentence.
why_open: No opened source explains why this particular leaf was left unfinished; absence of a proof here is not evidence that the problem remained open later.
worth: Worth using as the dossier’s organizing sequence; the sentence alone does not define a new theorem to pursue.

title: Write the categorical algebraic–analytic comparison
as_he_states: The margin proposes an equivalence for constructible torsion algebraic and analytic sheaves and says à rédiger.
plausible_today: Analytification identifies the algebraically constructible finite étale category with the corresponding analytic category having algebraic stratifications; arbitrary analytic strata are too broad.
state_of_art: SGA4 XI4 and XVI4.1 give finite-cover and cohomological comparison. The opened theorem XVI4.1 explicitly assumes proper f or constructible F. Stacks03RW specifies algebraic constructibility. A closed analytic exponential graph supplies the earlier run’s obstruction to arbitrary analytic strata, rechecked here.
why_open: No opened source explains why this particular leaf was left unfinished; absence of a proof here is not evidence that the problem remained open later.
worth: Worth an exact convention audit and comparison of the category statement with the published finite-cover theorem; the unrestricted variant is false.

title: The two relative comparison maps over an analytic base
as_he_states: For a finite-type relative scheme over a complex analytic space, prove both the displayed global-cohomology and higher-direct-image comparison maps are isomorphisms.
plausible_today: First specify a category of relative schemes over analytic spaces and its étale topology. For algebraic bases over C, finite type plus constructible torsion coefficients gives the precise established specialization.
state_of_art: SGA4 XVI4.1 proves the algebraic-base specialization with the correct properness/constructibility disjunction. Searches of SGA, primary comparison papers, and analytic/rigid literature did not identify the literal relative-analytic category and both assertions with these exact quantifiers.
why_open: The source itself has not defined the relative category; this is a formulation obstacle evidenced by the leaf, not a historical claim about why research stopped.
worth: Worth a focused bibliographic and definitional investigation; do not advertise it as a surviving open comparison theorem.

title: Continuity from analytic neighbourhoods to the local ring
as_he_states: After passing to the limit over neighbourhoods of y, the displayed analytic-local cohomology comparison should follow; the wording is conditional.
plausible_today: Combine an established relative comparison with finite-presentation continuity in a precisely defined relative-analytic category; retain the base-change map to Spec O_Y,y.
state_of_art: Stacks03Q9 Theorem59.53.1 verifies the corresponding algebraic strict-local continuity mechanism. SGA4 XVI4.1 alone does not establish arbitrary analytic-base continuity. No exact source for the full displayed conjunction was verified.
why_open: No opened source explains why this particular leaf was left unfinished; absence of a proof here is not evidence that the problem remained open later.
worth: Worth following jointly with MP-SA12-153, because changing the category or the limit changes the claim.

title: The rigid-analytic comparison hope
as_he_states: The relative comparison should also generalize to the rigid-analytic context, without specified field or coefficient hypotheses.
plausible_today: For an affinoid algebra A in Hansen’s setting, compare torsion étale cohomology of Spec A and Spa A; separate this from a categorical equivalence or arbitrary relative direct-image comparison.
state_of_art: Hansen, arXiv1708.07276 v1 (24August2017), Theorem1.7 proves the affinoid cohomological comparison for arbitrary torsion abelian sheaves. Its Conjecture1.8 concerns a stronger categorical statement. Huber’s1996 book, verified bibliographically, is explicitly cited by Hansen for the constant-sheaf and proper comparisons. The notebook’s unspecified generalization is only partly identifiable.
why_open: No opened source explains why this particular leaf was left unfinished; absence of a proof here is not evidence that the problem remained open later.
worth: Worth identifying the intended relative functor and coefficient restrictions before choosing which modern theorem or remaining question applies.

title: Complete the localization and support spectral sequences
as_he_states: Only headings for an exact sequence and a spectral sequence are written after the support functors; the edge consequence is used later.
plausible_today: For closed i and complementary open j, use the localization triangle and E2^{pq}=H^p(Y,H^q_Y(F))⇒H^{p+q}_Y(X,F), with the usual bounded-below convergence.
state_of_art: Stacks09XP §59.79 states the support formalism and spectral sequence. Hartshorne’s Local Cohomology, LNM41 (1967), explicitly derives from the Harvard fall1961 Grothendieck seminar, matching the dated margin at bibliographic level.
why_open: This is an omitted exposition step, not evidence of an unresolved theorem; the leaf itself cites earlier support-cohomology sources.
worth: Worth filling as commentary because it explains exactly how the later edge map is obtained.

title: Define the local fundamental class
as_he_states: Give the local fundamental class; later leaves supply the Kummer boundary of a regular equation and products for a regular sequence.
plausible_today: For a regular immersion i:Y→X of codimension d with n invertible, construct cl_i in H^{2d}_Y(X,Z/n(d)), compatibly with regular local factorizations.
state_of_art: SGA4 XVIII develops this construction; Riou, ExposéXVI §2.3, gives regular-immersion Gysin classes and their composition/excess properties. The codimension-one boundary is independently checked here. The initial request is partly answered within the same source.
why_open: The request is followed by an actual construction at22–24; the independence proof remains asserted rather than supplied.
worth: Worth treating as one developing construction across the leaves, rather than several independent open problems.

title: Absolute cohomological purity
as_he_states: Replace the smoothness hypothesis by regularity in the boxed absolute-purity problem, with qualifications involving good primes and resolution.
plausible_today: For a regular noetherian scheme X and regular closed subscheme Y of pure codimension c, with n invertible on X, the canonical class identifies Ri!Z/n with Z/n(−c)[−2c].
state_of_art: Gabber absolute purity is stated precisely in Riou XVI3.1.1. Riou’s introduction distinguishes Fujiwara’s2002 exposition from Gabber’s new proof announced2005; the seminar ran2006–2008, arXiv collection2012, printed book2014. The Fujiwara primary article was not successfully opened and is marked unverified.
why_open: SGA4 XVI3.10 and XIX’s introduction explicitly connect the historical limitation to resolution of singularities and distinguish equal-characteristic zero from the unresolved general case at that time.
worth: Worth a historical theorem-to-draft comparison; the stated invertible-torsion regular-pair problem is now settled.

title: Relative purity over an arbitrary base
as_he_states: There is also a relative purity theorem over an arbitrary base, with no full statement on this leaf.
plausible_today: For a smooth pair Y⊂X over S of pure relative codimension c and n invertible, the support cohomology is concentrated in degree2c and has the canonical twist; formation commutes with base change.
state_of_art: SGA4 XVI3.7–3.8.1, read in the opened full text, gives the smooth-pair statement and base-change corollary;3.10 identifies the twist using fundamental classes.
why_open: No opened source explains why this particular leaf was left unfinished; absence of a proof here is not evidence that the problem remained open later.
worth: Worth supplying the exact smooth-pair hypotheses; arbitrary regular pairs over arbitrary bases are a different assertion.

title: Extension to normal-crossing divisors
as_he_states: Extend the purity discussion to divisors with normal crossings; no formula is supplied.
plausible_today: For a strict normal-crossing divisor in a regular scheme and invertible n, compute R^qj_*Z/n from the degree-one Kummer classes of the local branches, as the corresponding exterior algebra.
state_of_art: Riou XVI3.1.3 gives the single regular divisor calculation and3.1.4 the strict normal-crossing exterior-algebra statement. Both result statements were opened.
why_open: No opened source explains why this particular leaf was left unfinished; absence of a proof here is not evidence that the problem remained open later.
worth: Worth identifying whether the leaf intends strict or étale-local normal crossings and fixing the branch-permutation descent.

title: Constructibility without properness
as_he_states: Expect the constructibility theorem for nonproper finite-type maps, with prime-to-characteristic torsion qualifications; later duality is used to obtain some ordinary-image constructibility.
plausible_today: For finite-type f:Y→X with X noetherian quasi-excellent, n invertible on X and F constructible Z/n, all R^qf_*F are constructible and vanish for q sufficiently large.
state_of_art: ILO XIII1.1.1 is the exact opened modern finiteness theorem. It circulated in arXiv1207.3648 (16July2012) from the2006–2008 seminar and appeared in2014. SGA4 XIX gives a historically narrower resolution-dependent setting. The scan48 partial-range shortcut is false (CL-SA12-678), even though the separate modern finiteness theorem is true.
why_open: SGA4 XIX’s introduction explicitly identifies reliance on resolution in the original argument; it does not explain every editorial decision on these leaves.
worth: Worth matching the finiteness assumptions to the draft and distinguishing the theorem from the failed partial-duality inference.

title: Independence from a regular sequence and admissible base change
as_he_states: The product class is said to be independent of the chosen regular equations; base change, intersection products and varying n are listed as properties, without their proofs.
plausible_today: The canonical regular-immersion Gysin class is independent of presentation, natural for Tor-independent base change, multiplicative for transversal composition/intersection, and compatible with invertible torsion coefficients.
state_of_art: Riou XVI2.3.1–2.3.2 supplies the general construction and excess formula, including zero-excess compatibility. SGA4 XVIII gives the published local/global programme. This review checks the divisor-unit case, not a complete reconstruction of the independence theorem.
why_open: No opened source explains why this particular leaf was left unfinished; absence of a proof here is not evidence that the problem remained open later.
worth: Worth a tightly scoped comparison of normalizations and signs, especially before using the classes in the trace diagram.

title: The point class generates top compact-support cohomology
as_he_states: A theorem to be proved will show that the rational-point class is a basis of top compact-support cohomology and independent of the point; the curve case is recalled as checked.
plausible_today: For smooth geometrically connected pure-d-dimensional X over separably closed k, n invertible and x∈X(k), trace identifies H_c^{2d}(X,Z/n(d)) with Z/n and sends cl_x to1.
state_of_art: SGA4 XVIII2.9–2.10 supplies the normalized trace and geometric-fibre criterion;3.2.5 yields Poincaré duality. The source’s rationality and geometric-connectedness qualifications are retained.
why_open: The text itself identifies this as a consequence of the forthcoming theorem, not a separate permanent conjecture.
worth: Worth using as a normalization test for the construction and for any comparison with the curve notes.

title: Existence and uniqueness of the normalized global trace
as_he_states: Construct the canonical trace for smooth compactifiable pure-dimensional morphisms, characterized by base change, composition, isomorphisms and the P¹ Kummer normalization.
plausible_today: For such f:X→S of dimension d and n invertible, construct Tr_f:R^{2d}f!Z/n(d)→Z/n; geometric connectedness and nonemptiness of fibres give an isomorphism.
state_of_art: SGA4 XVIII2.9 and2.10.1 are the exact opened construction and fibre criterion. Literal ordinary connectedness is insufficient, as the finite étale C/R example shows.
why_open: No opened source explains why this particular leaf was left unfinished; absence of a proof here is not evidence that the problem remained open later.
worth: Worth a proof-location and normalization audit; existence is established, while the source itself leaves the uniqueness argument unwritten.

title: Re-express the local/global class compatibility in the derived category
as_he_states: The corrected support/trace diagram will be expressed more easily and completely with derived categories; global duality is introduced as a title only.
plausible_today: For a regular immersion of smooth S-schemes, the fundamental-class Gysin map intertwines the smooth trace maps after the codimension shift and twist.
state_of_art: SGA4 XVIII2–3 and Riou XVI2.5.13 give the published trace/Gysin comparison. The overwritten diagram’s individual arrows are not certified as transcribed; the derived formulation is a stated reconstruction.
why_open: The source itself says the derived category will simplify the statement, providing an explicit editorial reason for deferral.
worth: Worth developing as a commentary diagram after checking the ink; it is an exact bridge between the local and global parts of the programme.

title: Flat resolutions for derived inverse image
as_he_states: Later notes will construct Lf* on D− using flat resolutions instead of projectives; finite Tor dimension is required for the stated boundedness extension.
plausible_today: K-flat resolutions define unbounded derived inverse image; exact pullback and finite Tor dimension yield the stated restrictions to bounded categories.
state_of_art: Stacks06YV §21.18 gives the modern construction. SGA4 XVII4 gives the classical derived formalism; the modern unbounded method is not attributed retrospectively to the leaf.
why_open: The text explicitly explains the issue: useful projectives need not exist, and without finite Tor dimension D+ is not preserved.
worth: Worth locating the promised later construction; no new abstract existence theorem is needed.

title: Realization of the allowed Coxeter diagrams
as_he_states: After deriving diagram restrictions, show all remaining possibilities are realized by finite reflection groups; the later root-system pages are to provide these realizations.
plausible_today: For the finite connected Coxeter types, construct positive-definite reflection representations; for crystallographic types use explicit reduced root systems.
state_of_art: Coxeter1934 §9 and the classification tables predate this draft’s likely period; received1933, published1934. Bourbaki Lie IV–VI (1968) is the later standard reference. The exact n°391 typescript identity and date remain unproved.
why_open: The source explicitly postpones realization until the classification candidates have been listed; this is exposition order.
worth: Worth connecting the nonconsecutive source pages in their original order and checking the omitted types, not treating the classical classification as an open problem.

title: Reducedness and irreducibility of the lattice shells
as_he_states: The lattice-shell criterion produces roots; reducedness and irreducibility remain to be checked in the concrete cases.
plausible_today: A finite spanning norm shell stable under the integral reflection formulas is reduced; irreducibility follows from the connectedness of the supplied simple-root diagram.
state_of_art: The exact rational program enumerates the E6/E7/E8 roots, verifies reflection stability and the connected Gram matrices, and checks the supplied simple-root/weight data. Bourbaki1968 and SGA3 XXI provide the published classification framework.
why_open: The deferral is a local verification instruction inside reused exposition, not evidence of an open research conjecture.
worth: Worth retaining as a reproducible certificate and as a way to detect numerical transcription errors.

title: Whether and where to define hyperalgebras and formal morphisms
as_he_states: The reused Tribu n°62 editorial sheet says it is undecided whether to define hyperalgebras generally and assigns formal-coordinate morphisms to another chapter.
plausible_today: This is a choice of exposition, not a conjecture that hyperalgebras exist. The antisymmetrized quadratic part of a formal group law defines its tangent Lie bracket under the usual hypotheses.
state_of_art: Bourbaki Lie II–III has a1972 original publication, verified bibliographically. Wehler2017 supplies a primary authored formal-group account, but the exact Tribu n°62 source and missing earlier formulas are unidentified.
why_open: The wording itself describes editorial placement and levels of calculation.
worth: Worth identifying the Tribu sheet and preserving the editorial nature of the question; not a new mathematical research direction.

as_he_states: One could add functor-of-points identities, square-zero tangent description and the sequence G(J)→G(A)→G(A/J); the final surjectivity is restricted to finite-dimensional G or open J. Add Proposition4(i),(ii).

state_of_art: Bourbaki Lie III is a verified bibliographic comparison; the unseen definitions of formal kernels and topological completed tensor products prevent an exact theorem identification. No unrestricted surjectivity is inferred from ordinary smoothness slogans.
